nodes.name: Carbonization for Cr-N-C
nodes.procedure: The isolated Cr-N4 sites on the mesoporous carbon (denoted as Cr-N-C) were first prepared by carbonizing the mixture of glucose (carbon source), dicyandiamide (nitrogen source), and chromium nitrate.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a schematically shows the synthesis procedure for the Pt-AC/Cr-N-C catalyst (details in the Supporting Information). Briefly, the isolated Cr-N4 sites on the mesoporous carbon (denoted as Cr-N-C) were first prepared by carbonizing the mixture of glucose (carbon source), dicyandiamide (nitrogen source), and chromium nitrate (Figure S1).

nodes.name: Wet impregnation and thermal treatment
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the Pt-AC/Cr-N-C catalyst was synthesized by anchoring the triphenylphosphine (PPh3)-coordinated Pt6 clusters onto the Cr-N-C substrate via a facile wet-impregnation process with subsequent thermal treatment to remove the surface ligand.

nodes.source_text: Subsequently, the Pt-AC/Cr-N-C catalyst was synthesized by anchoring the triphenylphosphine (PPh3)-coordinated Pt6 clusters (Figure S2) onto the Cr-N-C substrate via a facile wet-impregnation process with subsequent thermal treatment to remove the surface ligand.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image reveals 2D ultrathin sheet structure of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C without visible metal nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of as-prepared Pt-AC/Cr-N-C reveals a 2D ultrathin sheet structure without visible metal nanoparticles (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows coexistence of Cr single atoms and Pt atomic clusters (<1 nm) on carbon substrate with Cr atoms around Pt ACs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM was further applied ... The coexistence of Cr single atom (SA) and Pt ACs can be observed on the carbon substrate (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping confirms Pt ACs and Cr single atoms on N-doped carbon with negligible phosphorus signal indicating absence of residual PPh3 ligands.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM elemental mapping of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C further corroborates the successful construction of Pt ACs and Cr SA on N-doped carbon ... a negligible signal of phosphorus is detected, indicating the absence of residual surface ligands of PPh3 in Pt-AC/Cr-N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP determines Cr and Pt contents in Pt-AC/Cr-N-C as 2.03 wt% and 1.72 wt%, respectively; post-100h electrolysis shows <2% Pt loss.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cr and Pt contents of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C are determined to be 2.03 and 1.72 wt%, respectively, by inductively coupled plasma (ICP) spectroscopy ... the ICP test for the collected postcatalysts after 100 h of electrolysis shows a negligible loss (< 2%) of Pt atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-AC/Cr-N-C shows no metal-related diffraction peaks; Pt-NP/N-C and Pt-NP/Cr-N-C exhibit metallic Pt peaks indicating 3-5 nm and 2-4 nm nanoparticles, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Different from Pt-AC/Cr-N-C, in which no metal-related diffraction peaks are observed, the Xray diffraction pattern (XRD) of the Pt-NP/NC with noticeable diffraction peaks of metallic Pt indicates the formation of relatively large Pt nanoparticles ... The formation of crystalline Pt NPs is also demonstrated by XRD patterns of Pt-NP/Cr-N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr K-edge XANES negative shift and Pt L3-edge positive shift in Pt-AC/Cr-N-C confirm electron transfer from Pt ACs to Cr atoms via strong Pt-Cr coupling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a noticeable negative shift in the Cr K-edge XANES spectra is observed for Pt-AC/Cr-N-C ... Pt-AC/Cr-N-C shows more positive edge shift and higher white line intensity ... indicating the electron transfer from Pt ACs to Cr atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr K-edge EXAFS: Cr-N-C shows Cr-N at ~1.5 Å (CN=4); Pt-AC/Cr-N-C shows additional Cr-Pt at ~2.0 Å. Pt L3-edge: Pt-Cr1 at ~2.0 Å, Pt-Cr2 at ~3.8 Å confirming Pt-Cr bonding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CrK edge EXAFS spectra ... Cr-N-C exhibits only one peak centered at ~1.5 Å, assigned to Cr-N bonding ... a peak centered at ~2.0 Å, attributed to Cr-Pt bonding, appears for Pt-AC/Cr-N-C.

properties.description: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure Fourier Transform

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS: Pt 4f in Pt-AC/Cr-N-C (Pt0+Pt2+) shifts +0.5 eV vs Pt-NP/Cr-N-C; Cr 2p negative shift confirms Pt→Cr electron transfer. Post-electrolysis XPS unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS spectra of (g) Pt 4f and (h) Cr 2p ... the binding energy of Pt 4f in Pt-AC/Cr-N-C shows a noticeable positive shift by ~0.5 eV compared to that of Pt-NP/Cr-N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: OHads peak of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C at 0.69 V shifts 0.12 V lower than Pt/Ccom (0.81 V) and Pt-NP/N-C indicating oxophilic Cr-N4 sites promote OHads interaction; stronger HUPD peak shows increased H adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed OHads peak of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C (0.69 V) shifts toward lower potential by 0.12 V than those of Pt/Ccom (0.81 V) and Pt-NP/N-C (0.81 V) ... the underpotential deposition hydrogen (HUPD) peak of Pt-AC/Cr-N-C is distinctly stronger than that of Pt-NP/N-C.
